questions.question: In which country is the headquarters of the International Hockey Federation (FIH) located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Netherlands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The headquarters of the International Hockey Federation (FIH) is located in Lausanne, Switzerland, not the Netherlands. However, the Netherlands is historically significant in the context of hockey.
 
• The FIH was founded in 1924 and is the international governing body for the sport of field hockey and indoor hockey.
 
• Lausanne, Switzerland, is known as the Olympic Capital and hosts several international sports organizations, including the FIH.
 
• The Netherlands has a strong tradition in field hockey and is home to some of the world's top hockey teams. It plays a vital role in promoting the sport globally.
 
• FIH organizes major tournaments such as the Hockey World Cup, Hockey Pro League, and Olympic field hockey competitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India:**
 
 
• India is a powerhouse in field hockey and has won multiple Olympic gold medals in the sport.
 
• It hosted the Men's Hockey World Cup in 2018 and is scheduled to host the 2023 edition.
 
• The Indian Hockey Federation (IHF) oversees field hockey in the country.
 
 
 
• **England:**
 
 
• England has a strong hockey tradition and is part of the Great Britain hockey team that competes in the Olympics.
 
• Hockey in England is governed by England Hockey, which is responsible for developing the sport at all levels.
 
• It has hosted several international hockey tournaments, including the Women's Hockey World Cup in 2018.
 
 
 
• **Australia:**
 
 
• Australia is one of the leading nations in hockey and has won multiple Hockey World Cups and Olympic medals.
 
• Hockey Australia is the governing body responsible for the sport in the country.
 
• Australia's men's and women's teams consistently rank among the top in the world.
 
 
 
• **International Hockey Federation (FIH):**
 
 
• FIH aims to promote and develop hockey worldwide, ensuring consistency in rules and regulations.
 
• It works to expand the sport's global reach and enhance its popularity through innovative tournaments and programs.
 
• FIH is also responsible for setting standards for international competitions and the development of young talent.

questions.question: Which of the following is incorrectly matched with its description from the Preamble?

options.text: Sovereign - Independent in external and internal matters
Secular - Promotes one religion above others
Democratic - Government elected by the people

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Secular - Promotes one religion above others**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Preamble of India defines the secular aspect of the country as ensuring that the state does not favor or promote any particular religion.
 
• India is a secular nation where citizens are free to practice, profess, and propagate any religion or none at all.
 
• Secularism in India means equal treatment of all religions by the state and non-discrimination based on religion.
 
• The term “Secular” in the Indian Constitution highlights religious neutrality and separation of religion from the governance system.
 
• The incorrect pairing in this question is Option 3, as secularism does not promote one religion above others but ensures equality among all religions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sovereign**
 
 
• The term “Sovereign” in the Preamble signifies that India is an independent entity free from external control.
 
• It implies complete authority over internal and external affairs, allowing India to make decisions regarding its governance and international relations.
 
• This term highlights India’s autonomy as a self-governing and self-reliant nation.
 
 
 
• **Socialist**
 
 
• The term “Socialist” was added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 to reflect the commitment to social equity.
 
• It emphasizes reducing income and wealth disparities and ensuring equal opportunities for all citizens.
 
• The government promotes social welfare policies aimed at creating an egalitarian society.
 
 
 
• **Democratic**
 
 
• “Democratic” signifies that the government derives its authority from the people through the process of free and fair elections.
 
• In India, democracy is practiced as a representative form of government, where citizens elect their representatives to make decisions on their behalf.
 
• This term reflects the principle of popular sovereignty, ensuring the active participation of citizens in governance.

questions.question: The official language of Himachal Pradesh is ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindi** is the **official language** of the state of **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• It is widely spoken across the state and serves as the primary mode of communication for **official and administrative purposes**.
 
• **Article 343** of the Indian Constitution states that **Hindi**, in the Devanagari script, is the **official language of India**, and this applies to many states including Himachal Pradesh.
 
• **Himachal Pradesh**, being located in northern India, has a cultural and linguistic connection with **Hindi-speaking states** such as Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The state government uses **Hindi** for most of its administrative work, official documentation, and public communication.
 
• While **Pahari** and other dialects are also spoken locally, **Hindi** remains the dominant language for formal communication.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pahari**__
 __
 
• **Pahari** is a group of **dialects** spoken in the Himalayan regions, including parts of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• It consists of **several regional dialects** such as Kullu, Kangri, and Mandyali.
 
• Although widely spoken in the state, **Pahari** is not the official language.
 
• **UNESCO** has listed some Pahari languages as **endangered** due to the decline in native speakers.
 
 
 
• **Punjabi**__
 __
 
• **Punjabi** is the official language of Punjab and is spoken by a section of the population in Himachal Pradesh, especially in areas near the **Punjab border**.
 
• It is written in the **Gurmukhi script** and has a rich literary tradition.
 
• However, it is not the official language of Himachal Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Sanskrit**__
 
 
• **Sanskrit** is an **ancient language** of India and is considered the **mother of many Indian languages**.
 
• It has historical and religious significance but is not widely used in daily communication.
 
• The state of Himachal Pradesh has taken initiatives to promote **Sanskrit** education, but it is not its official language.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: If an image is formed at the same distance behind a mirror as the object in front, the mirror must be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**plane mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **plane mirror** forms an image at the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front of it due to its reflective properties.
 
• In a plane mirror, the image formed is **virtual, erect, and of the same size** as the object. This is because the mirror reflects light rays symmetrically.
 
• The image formed by a plane mirror is laterally inverted, meaning the left and right sides appear swapped.
 
• A plane mirror follows the **law of reflection**, where the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. This ensures symmetrical image formation.
 
• Plane mirrors are commonly used in households, optical instruments, and scientific experiments due to their ability to form clear and accurate images.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror forms **real or virtual images** depending on the object's position relative to the focal point.
 
• It is used in applications like **telescopes, headlights, and shaving mirrors** because it can magnify objects.
 
• When the object is placed beyond the focal point, the image is inverted and real. If the object is within the focal length, the image is virtual and magnified.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirror:**
 
 
• A convex mirror forms a virtual, erect, and **diminished image** irrespective of the object's position.
 
• It is widely used in **rearview mirrors of vehicles** due to its wide field of view.
 
• Convex mirrors diverge light rays, making them unsuitable for applications requiring focused light or magnified images.
 
 
 
• **Parabolic Mirror:**
 
 
• A parabolic mirror focuses light to a single point and is used in applications such as **satellite dishes, telescopes, and solar concentrators**.
 
• It is a type of concave mirror shaped to eliminate spherical aberrations, ensuring accurate focus.
 
 
 
• **Reflective Properties of Mirrors:**
 
 
• All mirrors reflect light according to the **law of reflection**, but the type of mirror determines the nature of the image (real or virtual).
 
• Plane mirrors are unique because they form images that are identical in size and shape to the object, making them ideal for everyday use.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Virtual Image:**

 
 
• A virtual image is formed when light rays appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror.
 
• Plane mirrors always produce virtual images, making them suitable for applications like dressing mirrors or decorative purposes.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Plane Mirrors:**
 
 
• Used in **periscopes** for reflecting light and providing a view of objects at different heights.
 
• Employed in **optical instruments** like kaleidoscopes to create symmetrical patterns.
 
• Commonly used for **decoration** and as household mirrors due to their ability to form clear images.

questions.question:
Match the following regarding Market Equilibrium:

 
 

 List I
 List II
 
 
 
 

 (a) Excess demand
 (i) Shortage at prevailing price
 
 

 (b) Excess supply
 (ii) Surplus at prevailing price
 
 

 (c) Price ceiling
 (iii) Maximum price fixed by government
 
 

 (d) Price floor
 (iv) Minimum price fixed by government
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **(a) - (i), (b) - (ii), (c) - (iii), (d) - (iv).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __**Key Points**__

 Market Equilibrium Concept (List I)
 Definition/Explanation (List II)

 (a) Excess demand
 (i) Shortage at prevailing price

 (b) Excess supply
 (ii) Surplus at prevailing price

 (c) Price ceiling
 (iii) Maximum price fixed by government

 (d) Price floor
 (iv) Minimum price fixed by government

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Detailed Explanation__

• Overview of Market Equilibrium:

• Market equilibrium occurs when the quantity of goods demanded by consumers equals the quantity of goods supplied by producers at a given price.

• It is a state where there is no tendency for prices to change, assuming other factors remain constant.

• Any deviation from equilibrium leads to either excess demand or excess supply, which influences the market forces to restore balance.

• Explanation of Terms:

• **(a) Excess Demand:**

• Occurs when the quantity demanded exceeds the quantity supplied at the prevailing price.

• This results in a shortage, as consumers are willing to buy more than producers are willing to supply.

• The market often reacts to this by increasing the price until equilibrium is restored.

• **(b) Excess Supply:**

• Occurs when the quantity supplied exceeds the quantity demanded at the prevailing price.

• This results in a surplus, as producers supply more goods than consumers are willing to buy.

• Producers may lower the price to attract more buyers and restore equilibrium.

• **(c) Price Ceiling:**

• A price ceiling is a government-imposed limit on how high a price can be charged for a product or service.

• It is typically set below the equilibrium price to ensure affordability for consumers.

• Examples include rent control or caps on the price of essential medicines.

• A price ceiling often leads to excess demand or shortages, as the low price encourages more buyers but discourages producers from supplying enough goods.

• **(d) Price Floor:**

• A price floor is a government-imposed limit on how low a price can be charged for a product or service.

• It is typically set above the equilibrium price to ensure fair income for producers.

• Examples include minimum wages or agricultural price supports.

• A price floor often leads to excess supply or surpluses, as the high price encourages more production but discourages consumers from buying as much.

• Market Implications:

• Both price ceilings and price floors are examples of government intervention in markets to achieve specific socio-economic goals.

• Excess demand and excess supply are temporary states that disrupt market equilibrium but also provide insights into consumer and producer behavior.

• Understanding these concepts is crucial for policymakers, businesses, and consumers to make informed decisions in dynamic market conditions.

</ul

questions.question: The 'Buland Darwaza' (Gate of Magnificence) at Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar to commemorate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**His victory over Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Buland Darwaza**, also known as the Gate of Magnificence, is one of the most iconic architectural structures built during the Mughal era.
 
• It was constructed by Emperor Akbar in 1576 CE to commemorate his **victory over Gujarat**, a significant milestone in his reign.
 
• It is situated at Fatehpur Sikri, a city founded by Akbar near Agra, which served as his capital for some time.
 
• The gateway stands as one of the **largest and tallest gateways in the world**, symbolizing Akbar's imperial power and architectural brilliance.
 
• The Buland Darwaza is an excellent example of Mughal architecture, showcasing a blend of **Persian and Indian architectural styles**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: His birth**
 
 
• Akbar was born on October 15, 1542, in Umerkot (present-day Pakistan).
 
• While Akbar celebrated his achievements through various architectural structures, no notable gateway was built specifically to commemorate his birth.
 
• His birth marked the beginning of one of the most remarkable reigns in Indian history, but the **Buland Darwaza was not related to this event**.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: His new religion, Din-i-Ilahi**
 
 
• Din-i-Ilahi was a syncretic religious philosophy introduced by Akbar in 1582 to promote religious tolerance and unity.
 
• This ideology aimed to blend elements of various religions, such as Hinduism, Islam, Jainism, and Christianity.
 
• While Akbar did promote Din-i-Ilahi during his reign, the **Buland Darwaza was not constructed to commemorate this religion**.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: His marriage to Jodha Bai**
 
 
• Jodha Bai, also known as Mariam-uz-Zamani, was a Hindu princess and one of Akbar's queens.
 
• Akbar's marriage to Jodha Bai was significant for promoting religious and cultural harmony during his reign.
 
• However, the **Buland Darwaza was not built to commemorate their marriage**.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Buland Darwaza**
 
 
• The Buland Darwaza is an architectural marvel that reflects the grandeur of the Mughal Empire.
 
• It is built of red sandstone, with intricate white marble and black granite inlays.
 
• The gateway includes inscriptions from the Quran, showcasing Akbar's interest in promoting Islamic traditions alongside secular governance.
 
• Fatehpur Sikri, where the Buland Darwaza is located, was a UNESCO World Heritage Site and holds immense historical and cultural significance.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Khudiram Bose was executed by the British for his involvement in which revolutionary act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muzaffarpur bomb attack**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Khudiram Bose was one of the youngest revolutionaries of India’s freedom struggle who actively fought against British colonial rule.
 
• He was involved in the Muzaffarpur bomb attack of 1908, which aimed to assassinate British magistrate Kingsford, known for his oppressive measures against Indians.
 
• On April 30, 1908, Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki threw bombs at a carriage they believed was carrying Kingsford; however, two British women were killed instead.
 
• Khudiram Bose was arrested, tried, and sentenced to death for his involvement in the bomb attack, and he was executed on August 11, 1908, at the age of 18.
 
• His martyrdom inspired numerous young revolutionaries across the country to join the fight against British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kakori Train Robbery:**
 
 
• The Kakori Train Robbery occurred on August 9, 1925, when members of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) looted government treasury funds from a train near Kakori, Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The robbery was masterminded by Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, and other revolutionaries to fund their armed struggle against British rule.
 
• It is considered one of the most daring acts of revolutionary defiance during India’s struggle for independence.
 
 
 
• **Chittagong Armoury Raid:**
 
 
• Led by Surya Sen (Masterda), the Chittagong Armoury Raid was an armed revolutionary act carried out on April 18, 1930, in Chittagong (now in Bangladesh).
 
• The plan involved seizing British arms and ammunition to ignite an armed uprising against colonial rule.
 
• Though the raid failed to achieve its ultimate goal, it inspired many revolutionaries and demonstrated the courage of Indian freedom fighters.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Assembly Bombing:**
 
 
• The Delhi Assembly Bombing was a revolutionary act carried out by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt on April 8, 1929.
 
• The objective was to protest against oppressive laws by throwing harmless bombs into the Central Legislative Assembly and shouting slogans of "Inquilab Zindabad." 
 
• The act was intended to make the British government "hear" the voice of Indian revolutionaries rather than cause harm.
 
 
 
• **Revolutionary Movement:**
 
 
• The revolutionary movement in India was a series of organized efforts to overthrow British rule through armed resistance.
 
• It involved secret societies, youth participation, and acts of defiance against colonial laws and oppression.
 
• Prominent revolutionaries such as Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, Khudiram Bose, and others played pivotal roles in inspiring future generations of freedom fighters.

questions.question:
Match the following connective tissues with their correct features.

 
 

 a. Areolar tissue
 i. fills spaces between organs
 
 

 b. Skeletal tissues
 ii. provide structural support and reduce friction.
 
 

 c. Ligaments
 iii. fibrous tissues that maintain muscle-to-bone
 
 

 d. Tendons
 iv. fibrous tissues that maintain bone-to-bone connection

options.text: a iv, b i, c iii, d ii
a i, b iv, c iii, d ii
a i, b ii, c iv, d iii
a i, b iv, c ii, d iii

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a i, b ii, c iv, d iii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Areolar Tissue:**

 
 
• Areolar tissue is a type of loose connective tissue that **fills spaces between organs** and acts as a cushion for support.
 
• It contains a gel-like matrix with collagen, elastic fibers, and fibroblast cells.
 
• It also provides a medium for the exchange of nutrients and waste products between the blood and surrounding tissues.
 
 
 
• **Skeletal Tissue:**
 
 
• Skeletal tissue includes bones and cartilages that **provide structural support and reduce friction during movement**.
 
• It protects vital organs, aids in locomotion, and acts as a reservoir for calcium and phosphate.
 
• Cartilage, a component of skeletal tissue, reduces friction at joint surfaces.
 
 
 
• **Ligaments:**
 
 
• Ligaments are **fibrous tissues that connect bones to other bones** at joints.
 
• They provide stability and limit excessive movement, preventing joint injuries.
 
• Composed of dense connective tissue, they are highly elastic and strong.
 
 
 
• **Tendons:**
 
 
• Tendons are **fibrous tissues that connect muscles to bones**, enabling movement.
 
• They transmit the force generated by muscle contraction to bones, facilitating body movement.
 
• Tendons are made of dense connective tissue with high tensile strength.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Connective Tissue Overview:**

 
 
• Connective tissues are responsible for providing **support, protection, and insulation** to the body.
 
• They are classified into loose connective tissue (e.g., areolar), dense connective tissue (e.g., ligaments and tendons), cartilage, bone, and blood.
 
• These tissues have an extracellular matrix composed of fibers (collagen and elastin) and ground substance.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Connective Tissues:**
 
 
• **Support:** Provides structural support to organs and tissues.
 
• **Protection:** Shields organs from mechanical damage and pathogens.
 
• **Binding:** Connects different tissues and organs.
 
• **Transport:** Blood, a connective tissue, transports oxygen, nutrients, and waste products.
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of Ligaments and Tendons:**
 
 
• **Ligaments:** Elastic, slightly extensible, and critical for joint stability.
 
• **Tendons:** Non-elastic and capable of withstanding high tension, enabling muscle movement.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Areolar Tissue:**
 
 
• Acts as a reservoir of water and salts for surrounding tissues.
 
• Plays a role in immunity by housing immune cells that combat pathogens.
 
• Prevents damage to internal organs by acting as a cushion and shock absorber.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Collagen and Elastin Fibers:**

 
 
• **Collagen fibers:** Provide tensile strength to connective tissues.
 
• **Elastin fibers:** Allow tissues to stretch and return to their original shape.
 
 
 
• **Bone and Cartilage:**
 
 
• **Bone:** A hard and rigid connective tissue, comprising collagen and calcium phosphate.
 
• **Cartilage:** A flexible and smooth tissue that reduces friction and absorbs shocks in joints.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book " Panchatantra"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vishnu Sharma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vishnu Sharma** is the author of the ancient Indian collection of interrelated fables known as the **"Panchatantra."**
 
• The "Panchatantra" is a compilation of moral stories that use animals as characters to convey life lessons and principles of statecraft.
 
• It was originally written in Sanskrit and has been translated into numerous languages worldwide, making it one of the most popular works of literature across the globe.
 
• The work is believed to have been written around 300 BCE, with the primary objective of teaching political science and ethics to three princes.
 
• These fables, divided into five sections or "tantras," are considered a masterpiece of ancient Indian literature and continue to hold relevance in modern times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhasa**
 
 
• Bhasa was an ancient Indian playwright who is considered one of the earliest dramatists in Sanskrit literature.
 
• His famous works include plays such as "Swapnavasavadattam" and "Pratijnayaugandharayanam."
 
• Unlike Vishnu Sharma, Bhasa's contributions are centered around dramatic storytelling rather than fables or moral tales.
 
 
 
• **Shudraka**
 
 
• Shudraka was an ancient Indian playwright and author of the famous Sanskrit play "**Mrichchhakatika**" (The Little Clay Cart).
 
• The play is a romantic drama interspersed with humor and political intrigue, highlighting themes of love, charity, and social issues.
 
• Shudraka's works differ from the Panchatantra as they focus on human emotions and societal norms rather than animal-based moral fables.
 
 
 
• **Kalidasa**
 
 
• Kalidasa is considered one of the greatest Sanskrit poets and dramatists of ancient India.
 
• His famous works include "**Abhijnanasakuntalam**," "**Meghaduta**," and "**Raghuvamsa**."
 
• Unlike Vishnu Sharma, Kalidasa's contributions primarily revolve around lyrical poetry and romantic epics rather than fables or teachings on political science.
 
 
</ul

• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• **Gorakhpur station** has one of the **world’s longest railway platforms**.
 
• **Lucknow and Kanpur** act as **major junctions for northern and central India**.

questions.question: The traditional dance form "Sattriya" originates from which region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sattriya** is one of the eight classical dance forms of India and has its origin in the state of **Assam**.
 
• It was introduced in the 15th century by the Vaishnavite saint and reformer **Srimanta Sankardeva**, who used it as a medium to propagate the teachings of Vaishnavism.
 
• The dance form was traditionally performed in the **Satras** (Vaishnavite monasteries) of Assam by male monks, known as **Bhokots**, as part of their daily rituals or as an offering to God.
 
• Sattriya incorporates elements of drama, dance, and storytelling, often enacting episodes from Hindu epics like the **Ramayana, Mahabharata**, and the **Bhagavata Purana**.
 
• In 2000, Sattriya was formally recognized as a classical dance form by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**, the national academy for performing arts in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tamil Nadu (Option 2) - Bharatanatyam**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It was traditionally performed in temples as an expression of devotion and was closely associated with religious rituals.
 
• The dance is characterized by intricate footwork, graceful movements, and elaborate expressions (*abhinaya*).
 
• It is performed to Carnatic music and depicts stories from Hindu mythology, especially from epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
 
 
• **Kerala (Option 3) - Kathakali**
 
 
• Kathakali is a traditional classical dance-drama from Kerala, known for its elaborate costumes, makeup, and storytelling.
 
• The performances are based on themes from Hindu epics, primarily the Mahabharata and the Ramayana.
 
• Kathakali is unique for its use of hand gestures (*mudras*) and facial expressions to convey emotions.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh (Option 4) - Kuchipudi**
 
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form originating from the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• This dance form combines graceful movements, rhythmic footwork, and theatrical performance.
 
• It is performed as a dance-drama and often includes dialogues and singing by the performers themselves.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In which year did the Union Territory of Lakshadweep come into being?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1956**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union Territory of Lakshadweep was officially formed on **1 November 1956** under the States Reorganization Act.
 
• It consists of 36 small islands and is India’s smallest Union Territory, both in terms of area and population.
 
• The name “Lakshadweep” means "a hundred thousand islands" in Sanskrit.
 
• The islands are located in the Arabian Sea, around 200 to 440 km off the southwestern coast of India.
 
• Initially, the islands were part of the Malabar district of the Madras Presidency during British rule but were reorganized as a Union Territory after India’s independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1966**

 
 
• In 1966, the Government of India established the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), which marked a significant step in India’s space exploration program.
 
• The same year, the Punjab Reorganisation Act came into effect, leading to the creation of Haryana as a separate state.
 
 
 
• **2000**
 
 
• In the year 2000, three new states were created in India: Jharkhand (carved out of Bihar), Chhattisgarh (carved out of Madhya Pradesh), and Uttarakhand (formerly Uttaranchal, carved out of Uttar Pradesh).
 
• This marked a major administrative reorganization aimed at better governance and regional development.
 
 
 
• **2019**
 
 
• In 2019, Jammu and Kashmir was reorganized into two Union Territories: Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, following the abrogation of Article 370.
 
• This move was one of the most significant changes in India’s political and administrative structure in recent history.
 
 
 
• **Theme of the Question**
 
 
• The question pertains to the historical reorganization of Indian states and Union Territories, which has been a key aspect of India’s post-independence governance structure.
 
• The States Reorganization Act of 1956 was a landmark legislation that reorganized boundaries of states and territories on linguistic lines and created several Union Territories for administrative convenience.

questions.question: How did the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Act, 1992, strengthen capital markets?

options.text: Providing statutory powers to regulate stock exchanges

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Providing statutory powers to regulate stock exchanges**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Act, 1992, granted SEBI statutory status, empowering it to regulate capital markets and protect the interests of investors.
 
• SEBI was given authority to regulate stock exchanges, intermediaries, and other participants in the securities market to ensure transparency and efficiency.
 
• The Act enabled SEBI to formulate guidelines for market participants, reduce malpractice, and ensure fair trading practices in the capital market.
 
• SEBI gained powers to investigate and enforce penalties for violations, thereby strengthening investor protection mechanisms.
 
• The Act aimed to curb fraudulent practices, insider trading, and unfair trade activities, enhancing the integrity of India’s financial markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Removing corporate tax on dividends:**

 
 
• This option does not relate to the SEBI Act, 1992. However, corporate tax on dividends is a separate financial policy decision aimed at encouraging corporate investment and growth.
 
• In India, dividend distribution tax (DDT) was abolished in the Union Budget 2020, and dividend income was made taxable in the hands of shareholders.
 
• This decision was unrelated to SEBI’s regulatory powers or the capital market reforms introduced through the SEBI Act.
 
 
 
• **Allowing unrestricted foreign borrowing:**
 
 
• This option is incorrect as it pertains to foreign exchange policies and external borrowing regulations set by the government, not the SEBI Act.
 
• Foreign borrowing is regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999, and is aimed at maintaining foreign currency reserves and economic stability.
 
• It does not fall under SEBI’s jurisdiction or the scope of the SEBI Act, 1992.
 
 
 
• **Abolishing stamp duty:**
 
 
• This option is unrelated to the SEBI Act, 1992. Stamp duty is a tax levied by the government on legal documents, including property transactions and share transfers.
 
• While stamp duty reforms have been introduced over time to streamline taxation, they are governed by state and central government laws, not SEBI.
 
• The SEBI Act focused on regulating securities markets rather than taxation policies like stamp duty.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme:**
 
 
• The SEBI Act, 1992, fundamentally transformed India’s securities market by establishing a statutory regulatory authority to oversee and protect investors’ interests.
 
• It played a key role in building trust and transparency in the market by regulating participants, enforcing compliance, and addressing malpractice.
 
• SEBI’s statutory powers marked a significant milestone in the evolution of India’s capital markets.

questions.question: NREGS was introduced to provide:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**employment in rural areas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS)**, now known as the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**, was introduced in **2005** by the Government of India to address unemployment in rural areas.
 
• The primary objective of the scheme is to provide a **legal guarantee of 100 days of wage employment** to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
 
• It primarily focuses on creating **sustainable rural infrastructure**, such as water conservation, irrigation facilities, afforestation, and rural connectivity through roads.
 
• The scheme is targeted at individuals in **rural areas**, ensuring **livelihood security** and aiming to reduce poverty by providing employment opportunities at the grassroots level.
 
• Through this scheme, the government intends to curb **seasonal migration** from rural to urban areas by creating job opportunities within the village itself.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Features of MGNREGA:**

 
 
• The scheme guarantees **employment to all rural households** who demand it, thus making it a demand-driven program.
 
• Wages are to be paid within **15 days** of work completion, ensuring timely income for rural workers.
 
• At least **one-third** of the beneficiaries must be **women**, promoting gender equity in employment.
 
• The scheme also mandates the use of environmentally sustainable practices such as **water harvesting**, **tree plantation**, and **soil conservation**.
 
• It is implemented by **Gram Panchayats**, ensuring local governance and decentralization of power.
 
 
 
• **Options Analysis:**
 
 
• **Option 1: Guarantee employment for women** – While women are given special emphasis, the scheme is not exclusively for women. Hence, this is **incorrect**.
 
• **Option 2: Guarantee employment for all graduates** – The scheme is not restricted to graduates but targets unskilled manual labor. Hence, this is **incorrect**.
 
• **Option 3: Employment in rural areas** – This is the **primary objective** of the scheme, making it the correct answer.
 
• **Option 4: Employment to all** – The scheme targets only rural households willing to do unskilled labor, not "all" individuals. Hence, this is **incorrect**.
 
 
 
• **Impact of MGNREGA:**
 
 
• It has significantly contributed to **poverty alleviation** and rural development.
 
• By providing income security, it has helped reduce rural indebtedness and improved the purchasing power of rural households.
 
• The scheme has also enhanced **social inclusion** by prioritizing marginalized sections of society, including Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and women.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts:**
 
 
• The scheme is funded jointly by the **Central and State governments**.
 
• It is considered one of the world's **largest social welfare programs**, covering over **260 million workers** in India.
 
• In **FY 2022-23**, the government allocated **INR 73,000 crore** to MGNREGA as part of its budget.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the allocation function of the government budget?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Providing public goods'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Allocation function of the government budget:**

 
 
• The allocation function is a core objective of government budgets, focusing on the efficient distribution of resources to ensure the provision of public goods and services.
 
• Public goods, such as defense, public infrastructure, education, and healthcare, are non-excludable and non-rivalrous, meaning that their consumption by one individual does not reduce their availability to others.
 
• Since private markets often fail to provide these goods adequately due to their non-profitable nature, the government steps in to allocate resources for their production and distribution.
 
• This function ensures that critical needs of the society are met, which might otherwise be neglected in a purely market-driven economy.
 
• Through taxation and public expenditure, the government collects resources from individuals and businesses and reallocates them to sectors that require public investment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reducing income inequalities:**

 
 
• While reducing income inequalities is an important government objective, it is primarily achieved through the **redistribution function** of the budget, not the allocation function.
 
• Redistribution involves using progressive taxation and welfare programs to transfer wealth from higher-income groups to lower-income groups to promote equity.
 
 
 
• **Maintaining price stability:**
 
 
• Maintaining price stability is associated with the government’s **stabilization function**, which focuses on controlling inflation and deflation to ensure economic stability.
 
• It involves monetary and fiscal policies to regulate aggregate demand and supply rather than addressing resource allocation for public goods.
 
 
 
• **Controlling imports:**
 
 
• Controlling imports is typically a part of trade policy and not directly linked to the allocation function of the government budget.
 
• This involves measures like tariffs, quotas, and trade agreements to balance trade deficits and protect domestic industries, which are distinct from the provision of public goods.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The allocation function is critical in addressing market failures, ensuring equitable access to essential goods and services for all citizens.
 
• It complements the other two core functions of the government budget—redistribution and stabilization—to foster economic growth and social welfare.
 
• Examples of public goods provided through this function include national defense, street lighting, public parks, and basic education.
 
• By efficiently allocating resources, the government also ensures that scarce resources are used in a manner that maximizes societal welfare.

questions.question: Based on the 2011 Census, identify the Indian state that recorded the highest percentage of Christian population.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagaland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the 2011 Census of India, Nagaland recorded the highest percentage of Christian population among Indian states.
 
• Approximately 87.93% of Nagaland's population identifies as Christians, making it the dominant religion in the state.
 
• The majority of Christians in Nagaland belong to Protestant denominations, particularly Baptists, which constitute the largest Christian community in the state.
 
• Nagaland is often referred to as the "most Baptist state in the world" due to the predominance of Baptist churches.
 
• The state's Christian population is attributed to extensive missionary activities during the colonial era, which played a significant role in spreading Christianity among the Naga tribes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mizoram:**

 
 
• Mizoram has a significant Christian population, which constitutes around 87% of its total population as per the 2011 Census.
 
• The majority belong to the Presbyterian Church, which is the largest Christian denomination in the state.
 
• Christianity in Mizoram was primarily introduced by Welsh missionaries in the late 19th century.
 
 
 
• **Meghalaya:**
 
 
• Christianity is a major religion in Meghalaya, with over 74.59% of the population adhering to it as per the 2011 Census.
 
• The Christian population in Meghalaya comprises mainly Protestants, including Presbyterians, Baptists, and Catholics.
 
• Missionary efforts during the British colonial period were instrumental in spreading Christianity among the Khasi, Jaintia, and Garo tribes.
 
 
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh:**
 
 
• Arunachal Pradesh has a smaller percentage of Christians compared to the above-mentioned states, with approximately 30.26% of the population identifying as Christians according to the 2011 Census.
 
• The state is religiously diverse, with significant populations practicing Hinduism, Buddhism, and indigenous tribal religions.
 
• Christianity has been growing in Arunachal Pradesh due to missionary activities, but it does not dominate the religious landscape like in Nagaland, Mizoram, or Meghalaya.

questions.question: What are the names of the official mascots for the Milano Cortina 2026 (6 to 22 Feb 2026) Winter Olympics and Paralympics 2026 (6 to 15 March 2026)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tina and Milo.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__Meet the Mascots__**

__
 
• **The Characters:** The official mascots for Milano Cortina 2026 (6 to 22 Feb 2026) Winter Olympics and Paralympics 2026 (6 to 15 March 2026) are two cheerful **stoats** (ermines) named **Tina and Milo**.
 
• **Tina:** The lighter-colored stoat is the mascot for the **Olympic Winter Games**. Her name is derived from **Cortina** d’Ampezzo.
 
• **Milo:** Her younger brother, the darker-colored stoat, is the mascot for the **Paralympic Winter Games**. His name is derived from **Milano** (Milan).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Symbolism__**

__
 
• **Resilience:** Stoats were chosen because they are resilient animals capable of adapting to harsh winter conditions in the Italian Alps.
 
• **Inclusivity:** Milo is depicted with only one paw, symbolizing **diversity and the ability to overcome obstacles**, which aligns with the spirit of the Paralympics.
 
• **Creative Origin:** The designs were inspired by ideas submitted by school children from across Italy, showcasing a bottom-up approach to the Games' identity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Quick Facts__**

 
• **Tina's Motto:** "Dream big!"
 
• **Milo's Motto:** "Obstacles are steps!"
 
• The duo is often accompanied by "The Flo" (six little snowdrops), representing the values of friendship and teamwork.
